Après les attaques du Hamas du 7 octobre: After the Hamas attacks of October 7 in Israel came the military response, still under way against Gaza, with the massive support of Jewish populations around the world. Yet within these communities there are dissenting voices that struggle to be heard amid the chaos of war and the noise of bombs. La Converse met Adrian* and Corey Balsam, two Jewish Montrealers, two voices for peace in Israel and Palestine.
<strong>« Israël, un pays qui existe pou: “Israel, a country that exists so that we can exist”
Douze heures avant la manifestation mont: Twelve hours before the pro-Palestinian demonstration in Montréal scheduled for October 13, Adrian, who grew up in Haifa, in northern Israel, opens up: “Tomorrow, I’ll stay home and I won’t join a possible counter-demonstration with my Israeli flag.” His reasons are clear: to protect himself and avoid exposing himself to antisemitic reactions. “Me, at any rate, I won’t be wearing my kippa over the next few weeks,” he says, speaking of the fear shared by many Jewish Montrealers.
De nationalité moldave, Adrian repense s: A Moldovan citizen, Adrian often thinks back to the day that put the Israeli-Palestinian question back at the centre of the news. “When I heard about the Hamas attack, I was surprised, confused and angry all at once,” he says. A call to a friend in Israel made him realize how close he was to the situation, despite the distance. “His girlfriend was kidnapped and still can’t be found. His other friends lost their lives at the rave in the Negev desert.” With no news of the young woman, Adrian assumes she is dead.
La réaction d’Israël, Adrian la condamne: Adrian unequivocally condemns Israel’s response. “I can’t find the right words to describe my emotion and my distress. I feel immense sadness for the Palestinians under bombardment and for the defenceless people of Gaza. They have no one to protect them. And even though I refuse to accept that my people be attacked or massacred, I know the Israeli response is disproportionate. ”
La colère et le chagrin d’Adrian se sont: Adrian’s anger and grief have also deepened with the surge in antisemitic acts: “In Australia, three days after the attacks, some demonstrators were chanting ‘Gas the Jews! Gas the Jews!’ I can hardly believe that in 2023 we are still facing such horrors. When I see that some of my Muslim friends don’t clearly condemn Hamas, I get the feeling that they could turn against me, that they could become the ones who, one day, would want to gas me. We haven’t yet turned the page on the Holocaust, and our grandparents who lived through it are still alive,” he says passionately.
Adrian marque une pause, puis poursuit s: Adrian pauses, then continues in a softer tone: “Many of us live in exile. As Jews, we are often faced with this question: who will protect us? Which country will be there for us? Canada? No! It won’t be there. We must not forget that during the Second World War, the deadliest period for Jews, Canada adopted the policy known as “<l1>None Is Too Many</l1>” to limit the arrival of Jewish refugees. All I know is that no one will be able to gas us as long as there is Israel, a country that exists so that we can exist.”
« Qui est responsable de tout ce qui se: “Who is responsible for everything that is happening? Who is responsible for this disaster?” he asks. The Haifa native, now 27, condemns Hamas, deeming the deliberate killing of Israeli civilians, whether children, men, women or the elderly, unacceptable and unjustifiable. But he points the finger at the Israeli government for its inability to find a way out of the conflict. “I condemn it too for the bombings on Gaza, but I can’t do more,” he says in a resigned tone.
Depuis le 7 octobre, Adrian oscille entr: Since October 7, Adrian has swung between anger and unanswered questions. “How could this happen? Israel is supposed to have the best army, the best security system. How did Hamas get around that iron wall, which, by the way, I find ridiculous? It’s supposed to be highly secured, with cameras, soldiers, sensors! Even a mosquito can’t cross those barriers without the Israeli authorities being informed. Did they underestimate the situation? Israel failed to protect us,” he exclaims, his voice full of frustration.
« Cette année, nous avons été témoins de: “This year, we witnessed numerous demonstrations in Israel against Netanyahu. This war will determine his future in the country.” Adrian nevertheless thinks it is too simplistic to blame only the government and its leader. “This problem isn’t new. Israel has historically supported a two-state solution and recognized the Palestinian Authority even before the intifadas, but Hamas refuses to recognize Israel.”
<strong>Sacrifier l’humanité sur l’autel: Sacrificing humanity on the altar of power
Ayant façonné une partie essentielle de: Having shaped an essential part of his identity by living in Israel, Adrian notes that people in the West seem far more radicalized than those who experience the situation up close. He points out: “There are Palestinians in Israel. There are Jews in the West Bank. Some are neighbours, sometimes even friends, on both sides. So the solution isn’t as black and white as that; there is much more nuance at the heart of the problem.”
Dans ce climat politique polarisé, Adria: In this polarized political climate, Adrian believes “we are always looking for enemies.” He feels that each side puts forward its own truth. “The Jewish people and the Palestinians refer to different periods of history to claim their right to the land, and in the end, there is no objective truth.” In his view, both peoples have a place in the Holy Land. He also criticizes the evacuation order Israel issued to the people of Gaza before bombing them: “Israel can’t ask Palestinians to leave, they have nowhere to go, because they’re home!”
Il conclut avec amertume : « Tout le mon: He concludes bitterly: “Everyone wants peace. However, history has shown us again and again that human life isn’t worth much. Innocent people die in wars waged by the powerful for power. The people who want war have no interest in seeing peace established. The people who want peace don’t have the means to live it.”
<strong>« Plus jamais ça » : Juif et con: “Never again”: Jewish and against the genocide in Gaza
Installé dans un café montréalais, Corey: Sitting in a Montréal café, Corey Balsam, a Jewish Canadian, sees the announcement of an emergency demonstration scheduled for October 17. Servers are talking about the latest bombings on Gaza. Corey asks them for a cardboard box to make a pro-Palestinian sign, on which he writes: “‘Never again!’ Jews against genocide.”
« J’ai participé à la manifestation aux: “I took part in the demonstration alongside thousands of other people to express my rage, my anger at the Israeli government and the situation of apartheid in general, but also at the governments of Canada and the United States, which seem to support Israel unconditionally,” explains Corey, national coordinator of Independent Jewish Voices Canada.
À propos du bombardement de l’hôpital ba: As for the bombing of the Baptist hospital in Gaza, Corey doesn’t know with certainty who is responsible. He remains sceptical, however, of information coming from the Israeli government. “I have no trust in Israel’s version of events in general. For example, regarding the journalist Shireen Abu Akleh, killed by Israeli soldiers in the West Bank. At first, they denied any involvement, blaming Palestinian gunfire, but in the end, the evidence clearly showed that it was indeed Israeli fire. Then they called it an accident,” he says. He doubts that armed groups in Gaza could cause such a deadly explosion. The conditions the people of Gaza are struggling to survive in trouble him. “Thousands of people have no food, no water, no access to medical care. People in Gaza are drinking dirty water or seawater. What is the Canadian government waiting for to act?”
Mais le plus douloureux reste la réactio: But the most painful part remains the reaction of his own community: “It saddens me to see a significant number of Jews support Israel’s plan for revenge. They refuse to call for a ceasefire on the pretext that Israel has the right to defend itself,” he says in one breath.
Corey Balsam, aujourd’hui papa, est auss: Corey Balsam, now a father, is also the grandson of a Holocaust survivor. “As Jews, when we say ‘Never again,’ it should apply to everyone. ‘Never again’ means ‘Never again genocide.’ It’s horrible to see Jews implicated in a genocide when we ourselves have suffered one.”
<strong>« On peut être fièrement Juif sa: “You can be proudly Jewish without supporting Israel”
« J’ai grandi en entendant l’histoire de: “I grew up hearing my grandfather’s story, which led me to develop a strong connection to Israel, a country that defended us. I also went to a Jewish summer camp where Zionism was strongly encouraged,” explains Corey.
Aujourd’hui dans la trentaine, il se déc: Now in his thirties, he declares himself “anti-Zionist.” Arriving at this ideological identity was a long and complex journey. “It was when I started reading about colonial systems, settler colonialism, occupation and apartheid that I began to see things from a new angle. It was very difficult and uncomfortable. I had to question everything I knew, everyone I knew.”
Sortir du sionisme a été difficile. Sa r: Leaving Zionism was hard. Meeting other anti-Zionist Jews helped him. “I didn’t even know that this possibility existed, that you could be proudly Jewish without supporting Israel, without supporting a criminal state,” he says.
C’est ce besoin d’avoir une autre commun: It is this need for another community that gave rise to Independent Jewish Voices. “Within our organization, there are people who are culturally Zionist, just as there are people who aren’t, but one thing is certain: Palestinians deserve better. We can’t support a government that commits crimes in our name.”
Au milieu des années 2000, Corey s’est r: In the mid-2000s, Corey went to the West Bank to live there and experience the reality of Palestinians up close: “I stayed nearly four years. I was around Palestinians every day and I was warmly welcomed as a Jew. Palestinians are kind, nonviolent people, far from the stereotyped image we have of them in the West.”
« Accuser systématiquement d’antisémitis: “Systematically accusing those who denounce their fate of antisemitism is ridiculous. Supporting Palestinian rights and calling for a boycott of companies that finance the war being waged against them has nothing to do with antisemitism. We won’t make progress by discriminating against supporters of peace in Palestine and labelling them pro-terrorist,” he concludes.
Ces entrevues avec Adrian et Corey ont é: These interviews with Adrian and Corey were conducted between October 12 and 18, 2023. As these lines are being written, communications with Gaza are cut off, and the bombings are not letting up. It is November 1. In light of this new reality, we called Corey and Adrian back to ask what they thought of the latest developments.
Adrian, visiblement préoccupé, nous décl: Adrian, visibly concerned, tells us the following: “No reasonable person can wish for the loss of innocent lives. I cannot in any way endorse the actions being carried out by the Israel Defense Forces right now.” Then, sincerely, he adds: “I want the Jewish people to be safe, especially in the context of rising antisemitism around the world. I hope the State of Israel can find its place in the Middle East. My heart longs for this war to end, and I pray for peace.”
Quant à Corey Balsam, il se mobilise, pr: As for Corey Balsam, he is mobilizing, taking part in demonstrations, vigils and sit-ins, sending letters to Prime Minister Justin Trudeau and engaging in other forms of civic involvement, doing everything he can to get one simple message heard: the call for a ceasefire in Gaza. “It’s a real disgrace! Both as a Jew, because Israel is acting in my name in committing these crimes, and as a Canadian, because our government isn’t taking a stand in favour of a ceasefire. It is undeniable that no military solution can bring peace. We are witnessing a genocide.”
